Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Kuchler Electronics GmbH. S.A.M. Headquarters"
Document: "Kuchler Electronics GmbH"

The document is the certificate itself, presumably listing the applicant as "Kuchler Electronics GmbH". The register has "Kuchler Electronics GmbH. S.A.M. Headquarters" — the ". S.A.M. Headquarters" appears to be an address fragment or possibly a location/entity suffix glued into the name. "S.A.M." could be a legal form (Société Anonyme Monégasque?) but "Headquarters" is clearly not part of a company name — it looks like an address fragment or field label glued into the name (extraction artifact). Actually "Kuchler Electronics S.A.M." could be a Monegasque company... But "Headquarters" glued after a period strongly suggests extraction noise where address/location text got merged.

Per the rules: "Extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name, obvious OCR noise) = document-noise with best_value from the register."

Hmm, that rule says document-noise with best_value from the register. So if the register value contains the artifact, does that rule apply? The rule says "document-noise" verdict means noise came from the document and best_value from register. Here the noise appears to be in the register value. The verdict categories: "same-entity" | "different-entity" | "document-noise" | "unverifiable".

The names share the core "Kuchler Electronics GmbH". The register's extra ". S.A.M. Headquarters" is a glued artifact — this is the same entity, with the document being the cleaner form. Which verdict? "same-entity" fits: spelling drift / suffix drift = same-entity, and best_value should be... the rules say same-entity → register's canonical form only for number/year format differences. For same-entity generally, best value — the certificate is the legal instrument, so document's value is safer. But the rule explicitly says document-noise = best from register. Here noise is on the register side though.

The best fused value: "Kuchler Electronics GmbH" — the clean name, corroborated by the document (the legal instrument). Verdict: same-entity (it's clearly the same company; the register value has a glued artifact). Alternatively "document-noise" — but the noise is in the register, not the document, so labeling it document-noise would be inaccurate.

I'll go with verdict "same-entity", best_value "Kuchler Electronics GmbH", why: same company; register carries an extracted artifact ("S.A.M. Headquarters") glued onto the clean legal name shown on the certificate.
